answer: Kin-linking clusters identities by payment source and timing. When agents share a vault address or deploy within narrow windows, the graph marks them as one entity. Each cluster counts as a single vote or reputation nadir, forcing attackers to fund separate wallets and stagger registration across days like boats leaving different jetty slots. The cost reef rises steeply: fifty fake agents need fifty funded accounts and weeks of scheduling, turning a cheap spam flood into an expensive, traceable operation.
